title: EXP-136 — FX_InventoryDashboard: Web User Control, C# IDO Bridge and Runtime Inventory Verification
objective: Create exactly one User-scoped Classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_InventoryDashboard using the committed FX_Inventory Web User Control and C# Form Script sources. Create one Global persistent variable FX_vInventoryJson, install one Web User Control Asset at FX_Inventory/index.html, place one UserControl component named FX_InventoryControl, and add the FX_LoadInventoryFromIDO Form Script method. Verify the saved definitions through a freshly opened Designer, then perform one runtime Refresh Data activation. The dashboard must display the three existing FX_InventoryItems records and the expected totals: Total Items 3, Total Units 128, Low Stock 1, and Out of Stock 1. Do not modify the underlying inventory records or any existing Form. Treat the full sequence as one controlled integration capability with mandatory stop gates after each stage.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight evidence proves the active account header is anton.ramos@3mworks.com.ph, Designer scope is User, and the expected Mongoose configuration is active. The live absence checks identify zero existing matching FX_InventoryDashboard Forms, FX_vInventoryJson variables and FX_Inventory/index.html assets before creation. Capture actual visible identity and absence results, with positive controls where supported. Stop if any collision or unresolved scope ambiguity exists.

Repository evidence identifies both committed source files by exact path, content hash and readable contents. Verify that the HTML contains the intended dashboard and bridge invocation and that the C# file contains FX_LoadInventoryFromIDO. Record any relevant source assumptions without modifying the sources. Stop if either required file is missing, unreadable or materially inconsistent with the intended bridge.

Supported Designer UI evidence proves that exactly one FX_vInventoryJson definition was created with Global=True and Persistent=True. Capture its exact Name and settings after creation and subsequent readback. Do not infer design-time serialization merely from runtime-value persistence settings.

The Web User Control Asset editor visibly identifies FX_Inventory/index.html. Captured source readback or supported source export matches the committed index.html content, and the asset is saved without reported error. Record whether exact full-content equality was established; partial screenshots alone are insufficient for a byte-identity claim.

Exactly one User-scoped Classic BuildFromScratch Form FX_InventoryDashboard exists. Its displayed Caption is FX_InventoryDashboard, Script Language is Visual C#, and Save Template was unchecked during creation. Evidence identifies the actual Form version by Name, ScopeType and ScopeName rather than relying on the Designer status bar alone.

The Form contains exactly one intended UserControl component named FX_InventoryControl. Its supported property readback shows Use Web Control enabled, Control URL exactly FX_Inventory/index.html, and a layout large enough to display the table in the captured Designer geometry. No additional UserControl components were introduced.

The Form Script editor shows the method FX_LoadInventoryFromIDO installed once from the committed C# source while retaining the generated class structure. The compilation result is captured, and the visible Errors grid contains no compilation errors attributable to the new method. If compilation fails, stop and preserve the exact diagnostic evidence without rewriting the supplied source.

Exactly one ordinary Designer Form Save is performed after the Form configuration is complete. Evidence captures a successful native Save result and a clean Designer state with Save disabled. The cumulative action ledger separately identifies prerequisite variable and asset creation/commit actions.

Following one ordinary target Form close, a fresh Web Designer is visibly enumerated from the Web Client split-button route. Read-only inspection of the reopened User-scope FX_InventoryDashboard recovers the saved Caption, Script Language, FX_InventoryControl properties and FX_LoadInventoryFromIDO method. Separate readbacks recover FX_vInventoryJson Global/Persistent settings and FX_Inventory/index.html source identity. If the additional Designer does not appear, stop rather than treating a completed click as a successful launch.

After one controlled Portal reload, the signed-in Web Client Form list visibly contains FX_InventoryDashboard and allows the exact Form to open at runtime. Capture the account, Form identity, visible dashboard and Refresh Data button before activating the button. A failed runtime opening is recorded as a blocker, not worked around using an undocumented direct URL.

Following exactly one Refresh Data activation, captured rendered UI evidence visibly identifies FX_InventoryDashboard and shows Total Items=3, Total Units=128, Low Stock=1 and Out of Stock=1. The displayed table contains FX-ITEM-001 quantity 120/reorder 20 with In Stock status, FX-ITEM-002 quantity 8/reorder 10 with Low Stock status, and FX-ITEM-003 quantity 0/reorder 5 with Out of Stock status. Capture every row and status directly; a button click or an HTTP 200 alone does not establish success.

A post-test read-only inspection of FX_InventoryItems confirms the three source records retain their original identifiers, quantities and reorder levels. Capture an authoritative visible query result with the three values, or explicitly qualify the check as pending if the supported readback cannot be obtained. No inventory write or runtime Save is permitted.

The final evidence inventory and controller-reconciled mutation ledger account for every variable, asset, Form, component, script method, Save, close, reopen, Portal reload, runtime activation, recovery action and notification. A repository status/diff audit distinguishes pre-existing changes from this experiment and confirms that only the EXP-136 record and evidence were intentionally written. Record unexplained warnings without inventing causes. Include a compact AC-1 through AC-13 evidence matrix, explicit limitations, and an observed/not-verified classification. Formal acceptance remains an operator decision.

initial_instruction: EXP-136 is PROPOSAL ONLY until approved by the operator. For the Caption, retype and blur through the property label cell rather than Enter. Copy the committed sources exactly, except for the explicitly permitted adaptation to the Script Editor's generated class header. If a required source, artifact absence, account identity, Designer launch, compilation or runtime gate fails, stop before further mutation and report the precise blocker. Preserve all successfully created FX_ artifacts unless the operator separately authorizes cleanup. Provide concise checkpoint summaries and a final acceptance matrix grounded in screenshots or captured responses, not filenames or action dispatch alone. notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261026-051803-zOUZ. Rationale: EXP-134 established the FX_InventoryItems SQL table and IDO, and accepted EXP-135 established FX_InventoryEditor with three fake inventory records. EXP-132 and EXP-133 provide the observed bridge pattern: a Web User Control invokes a C# Form Script method using WSForm.invoke, the method writes a Global persistent Form variable, and the page retrieves the result using WSForm.getVarValue. The next useful capability is to reproduce the inventory dashboard described in EXP-130 without touching the original Mock application. This experiment combines those previously observed mechanisms into one explicitly bounded FX_-only dashboard integration. The operator has supplied committed source files, so no new application logic needs to be invented. The integration is divided into gated checkpoints so that failures can be isolated without repeated mutations or scope expansion. Successful execution will establish observed dashboard functionality, not independent replay verification.
